_meta.description: Chess Theory Knowledge Base — index and metadata

opening_mistakes.description: Opening-specific mistake patterns with FEN matching, golden rules, and explanations
opening_mistakes.purpose: Power the Plateau Breaker Review page mistake explanations

endgame_principles.description: Endgame patterns matched by material count and piece configuration
endgame_principles.match_strategy: Material count + piece types on board
endgame_principles.purpose: Provide endgame-specific advice when mistakes occur in endgame positions

tactical_patterns.description: Tactical motifs and patterns detected from PV line analysis
tactical_patterns.match_strategy: Pattern type detected from Stockfish PV analysis
tactical_patterns.purpose: Enrich tactical explanations with pattern-specific rules and prevention tips

positional_rules.description: Generic rules mapped to PV line classification patterns (fallback)
positional_rules.purpose: Provide golden rules when no specific theory or tactical pattern matches

explain_mistake_endpoint: 1. chess_theory_service checks opening_mistakes.json for FEN + move match
2. chess_theory_service checks endgame_principles.json for material pattern match
3. line_parser.py parses Stockfish PV line for tactical patterns
4. line_parser.py maps detected pattern to positional_rules.json for golden rule
5. tactical_patterns.json enriches the explanation with prevention tips
admin_workflow: 1. Admin edits JSON files directly or via future Admin UI
3. New patterns are immediately available without server restart

separation_from_coaching_data.note: This knowledge base is SEPARATE from the live coaching data

coaching_data_locations.opening_plans.py: Deep opening teaching content for Play with Coach mode
coaching_data_locations.opening_teaching_db.py: FEN-based curated teaching for position-specific coaching
coaching_data_locations.verified_opening_traps.py: Canonical trap registry for live coaching

separation_from_coaching_data.why_separate: Coaching data teaches HOW to play. Theory data explains WHY a mistake was bad.
